headline: Use AI Sparingly, Prove It First
thesis: As EdTech Week wraps at Columbia, new warnings to ration classroom AI and scrutinize screen time meet fresh funding for teacher-controlled AI and student-safety standards.
summary: Pressure to slow down classroom AI keeps building: Australia's education research body urged schools to use AI sparingly and avoid it entirely in the first three years of primary school, while 150 clinicians called for health checks on edtech screen time. Meanwhile, builders keep building: Digital Promise opened grants of up to $600,000 for teacher-controlled AI, Georgia Tech landed $5M from Google.org, and Microsoft's AI safety and privacy standard with AFT and UFT takes effect for school contracts November 1. EdTech Week 2026 concludes at Teachers College, and Brookings' task-force findings remain the reference for the protect-before-scale argument. Direct access to most source sites was unavailable, so several sources are listed with evergreen items only.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · OCTOBER 16, 2026 · Direct site access was unavailable in this run, so items come from search results and secondary coverage and may not be the very latest; evergreen items are noted as such.

themes.title: AI Value & Evidence
themes.body: New testing finds AI models do the work but struggle to support learning, echoing calls to demonstrate impact before scaling.

themes.title: AI Policy & Backlash
themes.body: Australia's AERO urges sparing AI use in schools, following NYC's one-year pause on student-facing generative AI for Pre-K to 8.

themes.title: Student Protection & Trust
themes.body: Clinicians want edtech health checks, and Microsoft's AFT/UFT-backed privacy standard begins applying to school contracts November 1.

themes.title: Teachers, Faculty & Students
themes.body: Digital Promise's grants of up to $600,000 aim to give teachers more control over AI tools.

themes.title: Funding & Partnerships
themes.body: Google.org's $5M for Georgia Tech and Google Cloud's Gemini deal with Arden University show vendor money still flowing into AI education.

themes.title: Fall Events
